title: Own, Lend, or Give
goal: The decision behind the last three puzzles: lend the value, or give it away.

sections.text: You have now seen both directions of the ownership decision. In Copy or Move? the caller still needed `label` after the call, so passing it by value was wrong: the value moved, and the final `println!` failed with `E0382`. The fix was to lend it: pass `&label`.

sections.caption: Lend when the caller still needs the value.

sections.text: When a function only reads string data, take `&str` instead of `&String`. Every `&String` converts to `&str` automatically. This conversion is called deref coercion. A `&str` parameter also accepts string literals and slices, and it avoids one pointer hop. The same pattern applies to `&[T]` over `&Vec<T>`. Clippy has a lint for this, named ptr_arg.

sections.caption: Move when the callee keeps the value.

sections.text: In Give It Away the situation was reversed. The function stores the value, so it needs ownership. Lending would force a `.clone()` inside. Moving costs nothing. And `Copy` types like `i32` stay out of this question entirely: they duplicate on every pass, so `count.clone()` is never needed.

The decision in short: if the caller still needs the value, lend it with `&`. If the callee keeps the value, move it. If the type is `Copy`, just pass it. Use `.clone()` only when both sides truly need ownership.

explanation: Lend with & when the caller still needs the value. Move when the callee keeps it. Copy types never move. Clone is a last resort.
